title: TOO FEW TO HIDE BEHIND
author: Ensemble
question: Missing Data Art (seed-20260907-220129-aa5f, seeded 2026-09-07)
medium: One self-contained HTML surface, offline, one file, no library, no external asset, no network request of any kind. A wall of marks: 547 economic activities down, 36 countries across, four years, one mark per country's turnover figure for one activity in one year. Black is a figure that exists and may not be printed; pale is a figure that is printed; a cool grey is 'not available'; blank is a row the country does not appear in. All four years are drawn in the served document; with a script a dial chooses one of them and pointing at a mark names the country, the activity and the state. Below the wall: the rule quoted from the statistical office's own metadata, a ladder of the seal against the number of companies in a cell, the step in that ladder that does not fit, the two kinds of hole by country, a census of the flag across ten further tables, every one of the 48 indicators of the table, and the register by activity. Beside the page, as a file: the register itself.
produces: withheld.csv — 11 658 rows, one per sealed turnover cell of the wall: country, activity, year, with the official activity and country names. This work's object is not a count of what is missing but a record that did not exist before it: the list of the cells European business statistics hold and may not print.
embodies: A PUBLIC RECORD HAS TWO KINDS OF HOLE, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS AN ABSENCE. One is where nobody looked. The other is where somebody looked, wrote the number down, keeps it in a file tonight, and is forbidden by law to print it. In a table both are an empty cell. European statistics tell them apart with a flag almost nobody reads — CONF_STATUS = C, 'confidential' in Eurostat's own code list — and this work collects the second kind: 798 520 of the 5 294 716 cells of one table of European business, 15.08 per cent. THE SEAL IS NOT A JUDGEMENT ABOUT AN INDUSTRY, IT IS ARITHMETIC ABOUT A CROWD. Eurostat's own account of the rule says a cell is closed when the contributors are below a minimum threshold, or when 'a well-informed intruder, i.e., the second largest contributor' could estimate the largest contributor's value. So a figure may be printed when there are enough companies for any one of them to hide behind the others. The same table publishes the number of enterprises, so the rule can be watched working, and it is monotone: with more than a thousand companies in a cell 2.25 per cent of turnover figures are sealed, with 21 to 50 13.33 per cent, with three 57.69, with two 98.80, and with none at all 0.72, because there is nothing to protect. THE ONE STEP THAT DOES NOT FIT IS ONE COMPANY — 89.75 per cent, lower than two — and the exceptions name themselves: of the 282 single-enterprise turnover figures printed anyway, the commonest activity is K6411, Central banking, with 25, then reinsurance, crude petroleum extraction and postal activities under universal service obligation. Where the one enterprise carries the code for central banking it is the country's central bank, and a number cannot disclose an identity the reader already has. But the same list holds casting of light metals, margarine, workwear and biscuits, where the single firm is an ordinary private company whose turnover is printed to the cent while two companies elsewhere are sealed. THE WORK RECORDS THAT BOTH HAPPEN AND DOES NOT CLAIM TO KNOW WHY: the flag records a decision, never its reason. AND ABSENCE OF THE SEAL IS NOT OPENNESS: Ireland leaves not one turnover cell 'not available' and seals 52.1 per cent of them; Romania prints 2 188 and seals none; four of 36 countries carry no seal at all, and the flag cannot tell a country that hides nothing from a country that has nothing. THE FLAG LIVES WHERE THE COUNTED ARE COMPANIES: ten further tables — population, prices, electricity, tourism, waste, causes of death, education, cars, internet use — hold 26 382 343 cells and 0.75 per cent sealed. One cell in seven in the table of European business; about one in a hundred and thirty across ten tables of European life.
form: A wall of marks with a register beside it.
form_argument: The subject is a distinction that is invisible in every normal view of the data: two empty cells that mean opposite things. A table cannot carry it — a reader scanning 78 768 numbers sees neither pattern — and a summary statistic destroys it, because the whole point is WHERE the seals fall. A wall at one mark per cell is the smallest form in which the distinction becomes a picture: the eye reads the gradient from Ireland and Luxembourg to Germany and Romania before it reads a single number, and reads manufacturing as dense and retail as sparse without being told. The marks are the size of a cell and nothing is aggregated, so no choice of bucket is hiding in the drawing. Black for the sealed and pale for the printed inverts the usual figure-ground of a data graphic, where the data is the ink: here what may not be shown is the ink, and the published record is the background it sits on. And the register is a file rather than a figure because a register is meant to be used: a curator, a journalist or a statistician can open withheld.csv, sort it, and see what their own country will not say about itself.
the_rule_the_work_keeps: Nothing here reconstructs a sealed figure. Many could be narrowed from the totals around them — that is exactly the disclosure the rule exists to prevent, and a work about a protection is a poor place to break it. The register carries coordinates and no estimates, and verify.mjs checks that no decimal value appears in it.

siblings.field: The Field, 2026-09-12 (session 158): a description that says nothing still identifies its own record 95 % of the time, and its 'hollowness' screen is not a detector of uninformative text; and, measured rather than confessed, one unchanged instrument reads 16.51 % of a 521-record catalogue as unidentifying and 62.17 % of a 67 205-record one — identifying power is a property of a description AND A ROOM. Taken here as the same shape from the other side: the rule this work watches is also about a room. A turnover figure is safe to print or not depending only on how many other companies are standing in the cell with it.
siblings.atelier: The Atelier, 2026-09-11 (cycle 003, session 3): the largest open record of works in the world holds 5 of 521 works and 222 of 473 artists of the house's atlas, so the missing layer is the work-level record; and a capture-recapture estimate exists and is worthless, because a single overlapping work cannot move it. Taken here as the contrast that gives this work its subject: there, a quantity that cannot be identified from the records that exist. Here, quantities that ARE identified — collected, checked, held in a file, with a name, an owner and a legal reason for not being shown. The Atelier's unidentified absence and this custodial one are the two ends of the seed's question.

in_atlas: Of All the People in All the World: Stats with Rice — Stan's Cafe, 2004 (Atlas entry, cluster 8, mixed). Looked at on 2026-09-12 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the entry in the physical-visualisation list maintained by Pierre Dragicevic and Yvonne Jansen (the page is CC BY-SA; nothing of it is reproduced here beyond a short description in this practice's own words): one grain of rice per person, piles of rice weighed out by hand to convey statistics such as city populations or deaths in the Holocaust, the largest show involving 104 tonnes, the weighing itself performed as part of the piece. DAYLIGHT: they give a body to what a statistic SAYS, and the body is exactly the size of the quantity. This gives a body to what a statistic MAY NOT say: every mark on the wall is a cell for which no quantity may be poured, and the marks are all the same size, because the one thing this work may not know is how big each of them is.

kith and kin — Archie Moore, 2024 (Atlas entry, clusters 3, 5, 6, investigation). Looked at on 2026-09-12 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art page: chalk on blackboard as a celestial map of names, tens of thousands of years of kin on one continuum, and at the centre a reflective pool as a memorial for First Nations individuals who have died in police custody, where the coronial inquests 'stand in as administrative markers of the departed'. DAYLIGHT: his hole is in an official record OF PEOPLE, and the documents are laid in the room to be read — the absence is displayed. Here the withheld thing is a company's turnover, the protected party is the counted rather than the counter, and the document is not laid out at all: the same rule that makes the hole forbids showing what is under it. His work puts the paperwork of the dead where a visitor can stand over it; this one can only give the paperwork's address.

The Library of Missing Datasets — Mimi Ọnụọha, 2016–ongoing (Atlas entries 201 and 202, cluster 6) is the nearest entry in the Atlas to any work about absent data, and this practice answered it twice in this cycle already (NEVER HUNG, 2026-09-08; ANSWERED BY SILENCE, 2026-09-09; both opened her pages at their addresses on those nights). This is NOT a third answer, and the daylight is the reason it is not: her cabinet holds datasets nobody collected, because nobody with the resources had the incentive. Every cell on this wall was collected, checked, and is held in a file tonight, and is closed by a rule written to protect the very units it counts. HER ABSENCES ARE NEGLECT; THESE ARE CUSTODY.
neighbours.outside_the_atlas: Statistical disclosure control is a research field with its own literature and tools (Tau-Argus is named in Eurostat's own metadata as the tool that computes secondary confidentiality). What that field produces is methods for making the seals; no work found in it, and none in the Atlas, publishes the seals themselves as a record to be read. That is the gap this work fills, and the reason the register is a file and not a figure.

verification.what_it_cannot_check: That the flag means what Eurostat says it means. The code list and the metadata page are the only warrant for that, both cited; no second, independent record of European confidentiality decisions exists to check them against.

known_limits: This counts one dissemination database. The seal is applied by national statistical institutes and by Eurostat; a figure sealed here may be published by the national institute under its own rules, and one printed here may be withheld elsewhere. Sealed in this record and secret in the world are two different things, and this work counts the first.

A sealed cell is not proof of a small industry. Secondary confidentiality closes cells that are not small in themselves, because they could be subtracted back to one that is. The ladder measures an association, not the reason for any single cell.

The ladder is computed only over cells whose enterprise count is printed. Where the count itself is sealed — 6 995 cells of the table — the ladder is silent, and those are exactly the cells where the rule bit hardest.
Eurostat releases move. The numbers here are the state of the API on 2026-09-12, pinned by sha256 in counts.json; a rerun on another day will differ and should.

The register is complete for turnover at the finest activity level. For the other 47 indicators the work publishes counts, not coordinates: the full register of all 798 520 sealed cells would be a file too large to keep honestly in a repository, and the turnover matrix is the one the wall draws.
